reason: The text fragment demonstrates a Hebrew man actively and boldly expressing his views to Moses. When Moses confronts him about striking another Hebrew, the man directly questions Moses: 'Who made you a prince and judge over us?' (מִי שָׂמְךָ לְאִישׁ שַׂר וְשֹׁפֵט עָלֵינוּ). This shows Hebrew people freely voicing their objections and challenging authority, the opposite of being discouraged from expression. The consequences Moses fears stem from his killing of the Egyptian becoming known, not from any punishment of the Hebrew for speaking his mind.
